title: Give Your AI Agents a Live View of the Web
summary: Most agent platforms connect to SaaS tools. The live web is the gap. Here's how teams close it with Anakin - hospitality…
body_markdown:
AI agents do their best work when they can see the world as it is right now: current prices, fresh listings, live reviews. Not a static export from last quarter, or a spreadsheet someone copied by hand. Giving AI agents live web data reliably has been the hard part.


Most AI agent platforms connect to the software teams already run, like Gmail, Slack, Salesforce and Google Drive. Those integrations work well for structured data that lives in systems with proper APIs. But a lot of what agents actually need to act on isn't in those systems. It's on the live web: pricing pages, competitor listings, review aggregators, and professional tools that have no documented endpoint and no official way in.


Teams building on shared agent platforms like[Houston](https://gethouston.ai/) are already solving this. On Houston, a correction you give an agent sticks for everyone, and what the agent learns belongs to the company, not to any one person's account. Those agents still work best when they can pull live web data on demand. That's where Anakin comes in.


The short version: connect the live web once, as a tool every agent in the workspace can call, and workflows that used to stall on missing data start running on a schedule. Below are two that already do, then how the connection works and what it gives agents to work with.


## What teams are building


Both workflows already run on Houston. Each one used to take engineering time or manual effort most teams didn't have.


### Pricing intelligence for hospitality


Yield management, which means tracking competitor rates and adjusting pricing in real time, is standard practice at large hotel chains. For independent hotel operators and Airbnb hosts, it has historically meant opening five browser tabs every morning, copying numbers into a spreadsheet, and doing it again tomorrow.


The agent changes that. It pulls current pricing, availability windows, review scores, and demand signals from Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia, and Hostelworld, then writes everything to a Google Sheet (seven tabs, in[Houston's Revenue Manager setup guide](https://gethouston.ai/guides/revenue-manager/) ). The revenue manager opens the sheet. The manual work is gone.


In a business where margins depend on pricing one step ahead of the market, this kind of daily intelligence used to require dedicated tooling or a data team. Now it's an agent any team can run. Sometimes the only question is "did a competitor's rate move?" For that, Anakin's[Website Monitoring API](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/monitoring) can re-check the page on a schedule and send a webhook or email when it changes, with a specific_data mode built for price and stock tracking.


### Automotive pricing intelligence


A dealership with more than 1,000 employees needed the same thing for used cars. Pull current listings from AutoTrader, Cars.com, and a dozen competing platforms, aggregate them by make, model, trim, and mileage, and get that data to sales reps before a customer walks in and references what they saw online.


At that volume and frequency, browser-based scraping isn't practical.[Wire](https://anakin.io/products/wire) , Anakin's network-level extraction tool, handles it by intercepting the background API calls that each site's own frontend makes to load its listings. No browser to spin up. No rendered page to parse. AutoTrader and Cars.com both have ready-made actions in the Wire catalog, and the data comes back structured, so the agent can use it directly.


## How the connection works


**For technical teams** , the[URL Scraper API](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/url-scraper/submit-scrape-job) is a direct HTTP call:


```text
curl https://api.anakin.io/v1/url-scraper \
-H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"url": "https://www.airbnb.com/s/Miami", "useBrowser": true}'
```


The API is async: it returns a jobId, and you poll[GET /v1/url-scraper/{id}](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/url-scraper/get-job-status) for the result. The completed response carries the page as markdown and HTML, plus AI-extracted JSON if you ask for it. We ran this exact request on 25 Oct 2026. It took about 31 seconds and came back as markdown headed "Vacation rentals in Miami": Airbnb's own quick stats (27,240 rentals, a 4.7 average rating), about three dozen listing cards with ratings and review counts, and a month-by-month average price row. That row ran from $121 in September to $209 in March. Wire catalog actions use the same X-API-Key header and one[task endpoint](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/wire) , POST /v1/wire/task, with a distinct action ID per catalog entry.


**For non-technical teams** , the default for most agent builders on platforms like Houston, the entry point is a chat. Ask the agent to connect anakin.io and paste an Anakin API key when it asks. Houston adds it as a custom integration. Connect Anakin once. From that point, every shared agent in the workspace has access to URL Scraper, Wire catalog actions, Browser Sessions, Map, and Crawl. No API key per agent. No configuration per task. The person building the agent doesn't need to know how any of it works under the hood.


One connection per workspace, and every agent in that workspace gets access from there. Teams that work in Claude, Cursor or another MCP client get the same tools through an[MCP connection](https://anakin.io/blog/claude-code-codex-web-data-layer-anakin-mcp) . Either way, the agent instructions and operational knowledge stay shared and company-owned. The non-technical path has to hold up when a room full of people is trying it for the first time. It does.


## What agents get once Anakin is connected


Tool What it does


URL Scraper Fetches any URL - static or JS-rendered - and returns structured content


Wire More than 970 pre-built network-level scrapers for specific sites (973 as of 25 Oct 2026); scales without browser overhead

Together, these give agents roughly the web access a human researcher has, except it runs at whatever cadence the workflow needs and comes back structured.


## The ceiling most AI agent workflows hit


The hospitality case and the automotive case share the same structure: an agent needs to read something from the live web on a regular basis, that source doesn't offer a tidy integration, and without a solution the workflow stalls.


That's the ceiling most AI agent workflows quietly hit. The model is capable. The workspace is configured. The missing piece is the data.


A shared agent workspace handles how your team runs AI: corrections and skills accumulate, and agents get smarter over time. Anakin handles what those agents can actually see, which is the live web, at whatever frequency the workflow needs, without your team building or maintaining the connection.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Why do AI agents need live web data?


Most agent platforms connect to SaaS tools with proper APIs, like Gmail, Slack and Salesforce. Pricing pages, competitor listings and review sites usually have no documented endpoint, so an agent without web access ends up working from a static export or a spreadsheet someone copied by hand.


### How do Houston agents connect to Anakin?


Open a chat with your Houston agent, ask it to connect anakin.io, and paste your Anakin API key when it asks. Houston adds Anakin as a custom integration, and agents in the workspace can use it from there. Teams on Claude, Cursor or another MCP client can use the Anakin MCP server instead.


### What is the difference between URL Scraper and Wire?


URL Scraper fetches any URL, static or JS-rendered, and returns markdown, HTML and optional AI-extracted JSON through an async job you poll. Wire runs pre-built actions for specific sites (973 sites as of 25 Oct 2026, including AutoTrader and Cars.com) and returns structured data from the background API calls each site's own frontend makes.


### Can an agent track competitor prices every day?


Yes. The agent can run the same pull on a schedule, as the hospitality workflow does. If you only need to know when something changes, the Anakin Website Monitoring API re-checks a page, a site or a Wire action on an interval and sends a webhook or email alert. Its specific_data mode compares only the fields you define, which suits price and stock tracking.


### Can agents read pages that sit behind a login?


Yes, through Browser Sessions. You log in once in a real browser, Anakin saves the encrypted session state, and later requests reuse it to reach behind-login pages. Anakin's documentation states that passwords are not collected or stored.
